sources.title: Researchers used Claude to hack OpenAI

discussion.body: There's a dark comedy in Anthropic's safety tool being the one that cracked OpenAI's front door.

The more interesting point is structural: if an employee's ChatGPT account can expose private software internals, the risk isn't one company's tooling, it's the overlap between employee productivity apps and sensitive codebases.

original.title: Claude hacks OpenAI: Security researchers used Anthropic's tool to break into a ChatGPT account
original.body: Cybersecurity researchers broke into an OpenAI employee's ChatGPT account using software from Anthropic, OpenAI's key rival. The team gained access to private software information and even suggested changes, highlighting vulnerabilities in the ChatGPT maker's security posture at a time when leading AI companies face mounting scrutiny over safety. The researchers had been given access to an Anthropic tool specifically designed for security professionals, and were paid for the work as part of a program to find vulnerabilities before bad actors could exploit them. The episode is a reminder that the AI industry's competitive rivalry extends to offensive security: one company's red-team instrument became the lever against another's infrastructure.
